Plot temperature from Patch Reef 13 in KBay

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(purrr)
library(zoo)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
library(naniar)
```

Read in data from 2013-2023 (data obtained from Brown et al. 2023 - https://www.bco-dmo.org/dataset/905047)
```{r}
temps <- read.csv("../data/01-Environmental/905047_v1_infield_temp.csv", header = T)
```

Format date and time for data from 2013-2023
```{r}
# Create a date column for plotting
temps <- temps %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(paste(year, month, day, sep = "-")))

# Plot
ggplot(temps, aes(x = date, y = Temperature, color = Site)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Time (UTC)",y = "Temperature (°C)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Calculate DHW
```{r}
MMM <- 27.3
threshold <- MMM + 1 # 28.3

daily_mean <- temps %>%
  group_by(year, month, day) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(daily_temp_mean = mean(Temperature, na.rm = T)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::arrange(year, month, day) %>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(paste(year, month, day, sep = "-")),
    HS = ifelse(daily_temp_mean >= threshold, daily_temp_mean - MMM, 0)
  )

# Check if dates are continuous:
date_seq <- seq(min(daily_mean$date), max(daily_mean$date), by = "day")
missing_dates <- setdiff(date_seq, daily_mean$date)

if(length(missing_dates) > 0) {
  # Fill missing dates with HS = 0, daily_temp_mean = NA or interpolated
  missing_df <- data.frame(
    year = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%Y")),
    month = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%m")),
    day = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%d")),
    daily_temp_mean = NA,
    date = missing_dates,
    HS = 0
  )
  daily_mean <- bind_rows(daily_mean, missing_df) %>%
    arrange(date)
}

# Now compute rolling DHW (90-day window)
daily_mean <- daily_mean %>%
  mutate(DHW = rollapply(HS / 7, width = 90, sum, align = "right", fill = NA))

```

Plot! 
```{r}
# Define your MMM and bleaching thresholds
MMM <- 27.3
bleaching_threshold <- MMM + 1 # 28.3

# Create a date column for plotting
daily_mean <- daily_mean %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(paste(year, month, day, sep = "-"))) %>%
  mutate(DHW = ifelse(is.na(DHW), 0, DHW))

# scale constants (temp 20–30, DHW 0–10)
temp_min <- 20
temp_max <- 30
dhw_min  <- 0
dhw_max  <- 10

# scaling factor
scale_factor <- (temp_max - temp_min) / (dhw_max - dhw_min)

ggplot(daily_mean, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = daily_temp_mean, color = "Temperature"), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(y = DHW * scale_factor + temp_min, color = "DHW"), linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Daily Temperature (°C)",
    limits = c(temp_min, temp_max),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ (. - temp_min) / scale_factor,
      name = "Degree Heating Weeks (°C-weeks)",
      breaks = seq(0, 10, 2)
    )
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c("Temperature" = "steelblue", "DHW" = "firebrick")
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.title.y.left  = element_text(color = "steelblue"),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "firebrick"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

Plot with the points from temps
```{r}
MMM <- 27.3
threshold <- MMM + 1

# Prepare daily_mean with date
daily_mean <- daily_mean %>% 
  mutate(date = as.Date(paste(year, month, day, sep = "-"))) %>%
  mutate(datetime = as.POSIXct(date, format = "%Y-%m-%d", tz = "UTC"))

# Prepare hourly temps with POSIXct datetime
temps <- temps %>%
  mutate(
    datetime = make_datetime(year = year, month = month, day = day, hour = hour, min = 0, sec = 0, tz = "UTC"))

# Plot
ggplot() +
  # Hourly temperatures as light blue semi-transparent dots
  geom_point(data = temps, aes(x = datetime, y = Temperature), color = "grey60", alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5) +
  
  # Daily mean temperature as black line
  geom_line(data = daily_mean, aes(x = datetime, y = daily_temp_mean, color = "Temperature"), color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # DHW as gray line scaled to temperature y-axis limits (20-30)
  geom_line(data = daily_mean, aes(x = datetime, 
                                   y = DHW * (30 - 20) / (10 - 0) + 20), 
            color = "firebrick", size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  
  # Horizontal lines for MMM and Bleaching Threshold
  geom_hline(yintercept = MMM, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = threshold, linetype = "solid", color = "black") +
  
  # Primary y-axis limits and secondary axis that maps 20-30 temp to 0-10 DHW
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Temperature (°C)",
    limits = c(20, 30),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      trans = ~ (. - 20) * 10 / (30 - 20),
      name = "Degree Heating Weeks (°C wk⁻¹)",
      breaks = seq(0, 10, 1)
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
  geom_line(data = daily_mean_sub, aes(x = datetime,

            color = "firebrick", size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  
  # Horizontal lines for MMM and Bleaching Threshold
  geom_hline(yintercept = MMM, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = threshold, linetype = "solid", color = "black") +
  
  # Primary y-axis limits and secondary axis that maps 20-30 temp to 0-10 DHW
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Temperature (°C)",
    limits = c(20, 30),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      trans = ~ (. - 20) * 10 / (30 - 20),
      name = "Degree Heating Weeks (°C wk⁻¹)",
      breaks = seq(0, 10, 1)
    )
  ) +
  theme_classic()

```

Some data missing from 2019 and 2021. Supplement with temps from HIMB station
```{r}
temp_2019 <- read.table("../data/01-Environmental/mokh1h2019.txt", sep = "", skip = 0, header = F, na.strings = "NA")[,c(1:4, 15)]
temp_2020 <- read.table("../data/01-Environmental/mokh1h2020.txt", sep = "", skip = 0, header = F, na.strings = "NA")[,c(1:4, 15)]
temp_2021 <- read.table("../data/01-Environmental/mokh1h2021.txt", sep = "", skip = 0, header = F, na.strings = "NA")[,c(1:4, 15)]
temp_2022 <- read.table("../data/01-Environmental/mokh1h2022.txt", sep = "", skip = 0, header = F, na.strings = "NA")[,c(1:4, 15)]
colnames(temp_2019) <- colnames(temp_2020) <- colnames(temp_2021) <- colnames(temp_2022) <- c("year", "month", "day", "hour", "Temperature")

# Bind data together 
mokh_temps <- bind_rows(temp_2019, temp_2020, temp_2021, temp_2022) %>%
  replace_with_na(replace = list(Temperature = c("MM", "9   9.", ".0 999", "999", "0 999.", "999.0"))) %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(year),
    month = as.integer(month),
    day = as.integer(day),
    hour = as.integer(hour),
    Temperature = as.numeric(Temperature),
    datetime = as.POSIXct(sprintf("%d-%02d-%02d %02d:00:00", year, month, day, hour), tz = "UTC")
  )

# Ensure temps_sub datetime formatting matches
temps_sub <- temps_sub %>%
  mutate(
    Temperature = as.numeric(Temperature),
    datetime = as.POSIXct(sprintf("%d-%02d-%02d %02d:00:00", year, month, day, hour), tz = "UTC")
  )
```

Identify missing rows 
```{r}
missing_rows <- mokh_temps %>%
     anti_join(temps_sub,
               by = c("year", "month", "day", "hour"))
```

Append the subset data
```{r}
temps_sub_filled <- temps_sub %>%
  bind_rows(
    missing_rows %>%
      transmute(
        Temperature = Temperature,
        hour        = hour,
        year        = year,
        month       = month,
        day         = day,
        datetime    = as.POSIXct(
          sprintf("%d-%02d-%02d %02d:00:00", year, month, day, hour),
          tz = "UTC"))) %>%
  arrange(year, month, day, hour)
```

Calculate DHW
```{r}
MMM <- 27.3
threshold <- MMM + 1 # 28.3

daily_mean <- temps_sub_filled %>%
  group_by(year, month, day) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(daily_temp_mean = mean(Temperature, na.rm = T)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::arrange(year, month, day) %>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(paste(year, month, day, sep = "-")),
    HS = ifelse(daily_temp_mean >= threshold, daily_temp_mean - MMM, 0)
  )

# Check if dates are continuous:
date_seq <- seq(min(daily_mean$date), max(daily_mean$date), by = "day")
missing_dates <- setdiff(date_seq, daily_mean$date)

if(length(missing_dates) > 0) {
  # Fill missing dates with HS = 0, daily_temp_mean = NA or interpolated
  missing_df <- data.frame(
    year = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%Y")),
    month = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%m")),
    day = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%d")),
    daily_temp_mean = NA,
    date = missing_dates,
    HS = 0
  )
  daily_mean <- bind_rows(daily_mean, missing_df) %>%
    arrange(date)
}

# Now compute rolling DHW (90-day window)
daily_mean <- daily_mean %>%
  mutate(DHW = rollapply(HS / 7, width = 90, sum, align = "right", fill = NA))
```

Plot! 
```{r}
# 1. Filter data to the requested date range (July 1, 2019 to April 1, 2022)
start_date <- as.POSIXct("2019-07-01", tz = "UTC")
end_date   <- as.POSIXct("2022-04-01", tz = "UTC")

# Daily min/max summary for the temperature shading
daily_range <- temps_sub_filled %>%
  filter(datetime >= start_date & datetime <= end_date) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(datetime)) %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(
    temp_min = min(Temperature, na.rm = TRUE),
    temp_max = max(Temperature, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(datetime = as.POSIXct(date, format = "%Y-%m-%d", tz = "UTC"))

# Filter daily mean and DHW data frames
daily_mean_filtered <- daily_mean %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(paste(year, month, day, sep = "-"))) %>%
  mutate(datetime = as.POSIXct(date, format = "%Y-%m-%d", tz = "UTC")) %>%
  filter(datetime >= start_date & datetime <= end_date)

daily_mean_sub_filtered <- daily_mean_sub %>%
  filter(datetime >= start_date & datetime <= end_date)

# Vertical line date markers
vline_red  <- as.POSIXct("2019-10-01", tz = "UTC")
vline_blue <- as.POSIXct("2022-03-01", tz = "UTC")

marker_dates <- data.frame(
  datetime = c(as.POSIXct("2019-10-01", tz = "UTC"), as.POSIXct("2022-03-01", tz = "UTC")),
  color = c("red", "blue"),
  label = c("Oct 2019", "Mar 2022")
)

# Merge with daily mean to place diamonds right on the temperature curve
marker_points <- marker_dates %>%
  left_join(daily_mean_filtered, by = "datetime")

# 2. Plot
ggplot() +
  # Requirement 4: Grey DHW line with shading underneath (fill down to y = 20, corresponding to 0 DHW)
  geom_ribbon(data = daily_mean_sub_filtered, 
              aes(x = datetime, ymin = 20, ymax = DHW * (30 - 20) / (10 - 0) + 20),
              fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = daily_mean_sub_filtered, 
            aes(x = datetime, y = DHW * (30 - 20) / (10 - 0) + 20), 
            color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.8) +

  # Requirement 1: Temperature shading (min/max daily range) with daily mean line
  geom_ribbon(data = daily_range, 
              aes(x = datetime, ymin = temp_min, ymax = temp_max), 
              fill = "grey60", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = daily_mean_filtered, 
            aes(x = datetime, y = daily_temp_mean), 
            color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # Horizontal reference lines
  geom_hline(yintercept = MMM, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = threshold, linetype = "solid", color = "black") +

# OPTION A: Clean, subtle dashed vertical lines
  geom_vline(xintercept = marker_dates$datetime[1], color = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = marker_dates$datetime[2], color = "royalblue", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7) +

  # OPTION B: Diamond shape markers placed directly on the mean curve
  #geom_point(data = marker_points, aes(x = datetime, y = daily_temp_mean), 
  #           color = marker_points$color, shape = 18, size = 4.5) +
  # Formatted X-Axis (Every 2 Months, Angled, "July 2019")
  scale_x_datetime(
    limits = c(start_date, end_date),
    breaks = seq.POSIXt(start_date, end_date, by = "2 months"),
    labels = date_format("%B %Y"),
    expand = c(0.01, 0.01)
  ) +
  xlab("") +
  # Requirement 2 & 4: Axis limits & Fix right axis label symbol (using unicode \u207b\u00b9 for -1)
  #scale_x_datetime(limits = c(start_date, end_date), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Temperature (°C)",
    limits = c(20, 30),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      trans = ~ (. - 20) * 10 / (30 - 20),
      name = expression("Degree Heating Weeks ("*degree*"C wk"^-1*")"),      breaks = seq(0, 10, 1)
    )
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black")
  )
```















Calculate monthly means across non-heatwave years
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

# 1. Prepare monthly averages excluding heatwave years (2014, 2015, 2019)
monthly_climatology <- temps %>%
  mutate(
    year  = year(datetime),
    month = month(datetime)
  ) %>%
  # Exclude known heatwave years to establish baseline
  filter(!year %in% c(2014, 2015, 2019)) %>%
  
  # Step A: Compute mean temperature for each year-month combination
  group_by(year, month) %>%
  summarize(monthly_mean = mean(Temperature, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  # Step B: Average monthly means across non-heatwave years
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarize(climatological_monthly_mean = mean(monthly_mean, na.rm = TRUE))

# 2. Identify the warmest month and extract local MMM
local_MMM_df <- monthly_climatology %>%
  filter(climatological_monthly_mean == max(climatological_monthly_mean))

local_MMM <- local_MMM_df$climatological_monthly_mean
local_threshold <- local_MMM + 1.0

cat("Warmest Month:", local_MMM_df$month, "\n")
cat("Local Site MMM:", round(local_MMM, 2), "°C\n")
cat("Local Bleaching Threshold (MMM + 1):", round(local_threshold, 2), "°C\n")

# Daily climatology from non-heatwave years
daily_climatology <- temps %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(datetime),
    yday = yday(datetime) # day of year (1-366)
  ) %>%
  filter(!year %in% c(2014, 2015, 2019)) %>%
  group_by(yday) %>%
  summarize(mean_day_temp = mean(Temperature, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  
  # Smooth with a 31-day window
  mutate(smoothed_climatology = zoo::rollapply(mean_day_temp, width = 31, FUN = mean, fill = "extend", align = "center"))

# Local MMM is the peak of the smoothed seasonal cycle
local_MMM_daily <- max(daily_climatology$smoothed_climatology, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Local Daily Climatology Peak MMM:", round(local_MMM_daily, 2), "°C\n")
```


















Read in data from hobo loggers from NSF CAREER project. These are all in different formats so they need to be read in and processed differently. 
```{r}

  mutate(DateTime = dmy_hms(paste(Date, Time..GMT.10.00)),
         Temp_C = Temp...C) %>%
  dplyr::select(DateTime, Temp_C)
```

Bind all data together, save and plot 
```{r}
all_data <- rbind(sept22_apr23, apr23_sept23, sept23_jan24, jan24_may24, may24_sept24, oct24_jan25, jan25_may25, may25_oct25, oct25_jan26, jan26_may26, may26_oct26)

# Write csv
write.csv(all_data, "../output/01-Environmental/NSF_CAREER_KBay_PR13_Temps.csv")

ggplot(all_data, aes(x = DateTime, y = Temp_C)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_datetime( date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(y = "Temperature (°C)", x = "Time")
```

Separate out year, month and day 
```{r}
all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(DateTime),
    month = month(DateTime),
    day = day(DateTime),
    hour = hour(DateTime))
```

Calculate DHW
```{r}
daily_mean_nsf <- all_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year, month, day) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(daily_temp_mean = mean(Temp_C, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  dplyr::arrange(year, month, day) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    date = as.Date(paste(year, month, day, sep = "-")),
    HS = ifelse(daily_temp_mean >= threshold, daily_temp_mean - MMM, 0)
  )

# Check if dates are continuous:
date_seq <- seq(min(daily_mean_nsf$date), max(daily_mean_nsf$date), by = "day")
missing_dates <- setdiff(date_seq, daily_mean_nsf$date)

if(length(missing_dates) > 0) {
  # Fill missing dates with HS = 0, daily_temp_mean = NA or interpolated
  missing_df <- data.frame(
    year = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%Y")),
    month = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%m")),
    day = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%d")),
    daily_temp_mean = NA,
    date = missing_dates,
    HS = 0
  )
  daily_mean_nsf <- bind_rows(daily_mean_nsf, missing_df) %>%
    arrange(date)
}

# Now compute rolling DHW (90-day window)
daily_mean_nsf <- daily_mean_nsf %>%
  mutate(DHW = rollapply(HS / 7, width = 90, sum, align = "right", fill = NA))
```

Plot! 
```{r}
# Define your MMM and bleaching thresholds
MMM <- 27.3
threshold <- MMM + 1 # 28.3

# Create a date column for plotting
daily_mean_nsf <- daily_mean_nsf %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(paste(year, month, day, sep = "-"))) %>%
  mutate(DHW = ifelse(is.na(DHW), 0, DHW))

# scale constants (temp 20–30, DHW 0–10)
temp_min <- 20
temp_max <- 30
dhw_min  <- 0
dhw_max  <- 10

# scaling factor
scale_factor <- (temp_max - temp_min) / (dhw_max - dhw_min)

ggplot(daily_mean_nsf, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = daily_temp_mean, color = "Temperature"), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(y = DHW * scale_factor + temp_min, color = "DHW"), linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Daily Temperature (°C)",
    limits = c(temp_min, temp_max),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ (. - temp_min) / scale_factor,
      name = "Degree Heating Weeks (°C-weeks)",
      breaks = seq(0, 10, 2)
    )
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c("Temperature" = "steelblue", "DHW" = "firebrick")
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.title.y.left  = element_text(color = "steelblue"),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "firebrick"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

Plot with the points from hourly data
```{r}
MMM <- 27.3
threshold <- MMM + 1

# Prepare daily_mean with date
daily_mean_nsf <- daily_mean_nsf %>% 
  mutate(date = as.Date(paste(year, month, day, sep = "-"))) %>%
  mutate(datetime = as.POSIXct(date, format = "%Y-%m-%d", tz = "UTC"))

# Prepare hourly temps with POSIXct datetime
all_data$year <- as.integer(all_data$year)
all_data$month <- as.integer(all_data$month)
all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(
    datetime = make_datetime(year = year, month = month, day = day, hour = hour, tz = "UTC"))

# Plot
ggplot() +
  # Hourly temperatures as light blue semi-transparent dots
  geom_point(data = all_data, aes(x = datetime, y = Temp_C), color = "grey60", alpha = 0.3, size = 0.5) +
  
  # Daily mean temperature as black line
  geom_line(data = daily_mean_nsf, aes(x = datetime, y = daily_temp_mean, color = "Temperature"), color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # DHW as gray line scaled to temperature y-axis limits (20-30)
  geom_line(data = daily_mean_nsf, aes(x = datetime,
                                   y = DHW * (30 - 20) / (10 - 0) + 20),
            color = "firebrick", size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  
  # Horizontal lines for MMM and Bleaching Threshold
  geom_hline(yintercept = MMM, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = threshold, linetype = "solid", color = "black") +
  
  # Primary y-axis limits and secondary axis that maps 20-30 temp to 0-10 DHW
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Temperature (°C)",
    limits = c(20, 30),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      trans = ~ (. - 20) * 10 / (30 - 20),
      name = "Degree Heating Weeks (°C/week)",
      breaks = seq(0, 10, 1)
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


### Combine 

Select and rename specific cols 
```{r}
temps_sub <- temps %>%
  dplyr::select(Temperature, hour, year, day, month, datetime) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Temperature = Temperature,  # already named correctly, just for clarity
         hour = hour,
         year = year,
         month = month,
         day = day,
         datetime = datetime)

all_data_sub <- all_data %>%
  dplyr::rename(Temperature = Temp_C) %>%
  dplyr::select(Temperature, hour, year, month, day, datetime)

# Reorder columns in temps_sub to match all_data_sub
temps_sub <- temps_sub %>%
  dplyr::select(Temperature, hour, year, month, day, datetime)

# Bind
combined_data <- bind_rows(temps_sub, all_data_sub)
```

Calculate DHW
```{r}
daily_mean <- combined_data %>%
  group_by(year, month, day) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(daily_temp_mean = mean(Temperature, na.rm = T)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::arrange(year, month, day) %>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(paste(year, month, day, sep = "-")),
    HS = ifelse(daily_temp_mean >= threshold, daily_temp_mean - MMM, 0)
  )

# Check if dates are continuous:
date_seq <- seq(min(daily_mean$date), max(daily_mean$date), by = "day")
missing_dates <- setdiff(date_seq, daily_mean$date)

if(length(missing_dates) > 0) {
  # Fill missing dates with HS = 0, daily_temp_mean = NA or interpolated
  missing_df <- data.frame(
    year = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%Y")),
    month = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%m")),
    day = as.integer(format(missing_dates, "%d")),
    daily_temp_mean = NA,
    date = missing_dates,
    HS = 0
  )
  daily_mean <- bind_rows(daily_mean, missing_df) %>%
    arrange(date)
}

# Now compute rolling DHW (90-day window)
daily_mean <- daily_mean %>%
  mutate(DHW = rollapply(HS / 7, width = 90, sum, align = "right", fill = NA))
```

Calculate the avg temp for the week and day prior to sampling dates 
```{r}
# make sure datetime columns are POSIXct
all_data <- all_data %>%
  mutate(datetime = ymd_hms(datetime))

sample_dates <- sample_dates %>%
  mutate(datetime = ymd(datetime))

# function to calculate mean + sem + n
calc_stats <- function(data, start_date, end_date, sample_id, window) {
  df <- data %>%
    filter(datetime >= start_date & datetime < end_date)
  
  if(nrow(df) > 0) {
    mean_val <- mean(df$Temp_C, na.rm = TRUE)
    sem_val  <- sd(df$Temp_C, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(df$Temp_C)))
    n_val    <- sum(!is.na(df$Temp_C))
  } else {
    mean_val <- NA
    sem_val  <- NA
    n_val    <- 0
  }
  
  tibble(
    sample_id = sample_id,
    window = window,
    mean_temp = mean_val,
    sem_temp = sem_val,
    n = n_val
  )
}

# loop over sample_dates and calculate stats for week, day, month
results <- purrr::map_dfr(1:nrow(sample_dates), function(i) {
  samp_date <- sample_dates$datetime[i]
  samp_id   <- sample_dates$sample_id[i]
  
  week_prior_start  <- samp_date - days(7)
  day_prior_start   <- samp_date - days(2)
  month_prior_start <- samp_date - days(30)
  
  bind_rows(
    calc_stats(all_data, week_prior_start, samp_date, samp_id, "week_prior"),
    calc_stats(all_data, day_prior_start, samp_date, samp_id, "day_prior"),
    calc_stats(all_data, month_prior_start, samp_date, samp_id, "month_prior")
  )
})

results

```

Plot 2023 and 2025
```{r}
# 1. Setup Collection Dates and Combine Data
temps_2023$Collection_Date <- as.POSIXct("2023-09-23")
temps_2025$Collection_Date <- as.POSIXct("2025-10-01")

all_temps <- bind_rows(
  temps_2023 %>% mutate(Sampling_Year = "2023"),
  temps_2025 %>% mutate(Sampling_Year = "2025")
) %>%
  mutate(
    DateTime = as.POSIXct(DateTime),
    Days_Before = as.numeric(difftime(DateTime, Collection_Date, units = "days"))
  ) %>%
  filter(Days_Before >= -365 & Days_Before <= 0)

# Define New Colors (Teal and Gold)
env_colors <- c("2023" = "#008080", "2025" = "#D4AF37")

# PANEL A 
p_time <- ggplot(all_temps, aes(x = Days_Before, y = Temp_C, color = Sampling_Year)) +
   geom_hline(yintercept = 28, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", alpha = 0.5) +
   geom_line(alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
   geom_smooth(method = "gam", linewidth = 1.4, se = FALSE) +
   scale_color_manual(values = env_colors) +
   
   # ADD na.rm = TRUE here to handle missing data
   scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(floor(min(all_temps$Temp_C, na.rm = TRUE)), 
                                   ceiling(max(all_temps$Temp_C, na.rm = TRUE)), by = 2)) +
   
   theme_classic() +
   theme(
     axis.text = element_text(size = 15, color = "black"),
     axis.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "plain"),
     legend.position = "none" 
   ) +
   labs(x = "Days Before Collection", y = "Temperature (°C)")

# PANEL B: Frequency as Percentage (Right)
freq_data <- all_temps %>%
  mutate(temp_bin = round(Temp_C)) %>%
  group_by(Sampling_Year, temp_bin) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  mutate(percent = (count / sum(count)) * 100)

p_freq <- ggplot(freq_data, aes(x = temp_bin, y = percent, fill = Sampling_Year)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", alpha = 0.85, color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = env_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(22, 32, 1)) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 15, color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "plain"),
    legend.position = "right", 
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(x = "Temperature Bin (°C)", 
       y = "Percentage of Total Time (%)", 
       fill = "Year")

# 3. Assemble Side-by-Side and Label with Patchwork
# plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A') automatically labels the plots
final_env_plot <- (p_time + p_freq) + 
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.3, 1)) + 
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = 'A') & 
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

# Save 
ggsave("../output/environmental/Temperatures_2023_and_2025.pdf", 
       plot = final_env_plot, 
       width = 18, 
       height = 6, 
       units = "in", 
       device = "pdf",
       dpi = 300)
ggsave("../output/environmental/Temperatures_2023_and_2025.png", 
       plot = final_env_plot, 
       width = 18, 
       height = 6, 
       units = "in", 
       dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
combined_data$datetime <- as.POSIXct(combined_data$datetime)
```

Calculate numbers of days above MMM and MMM+1
```{r}
compare_temps <- combined_data %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2019, 2023, 2025),
         month >= 3 & month <= 10) 

# Calculate hourly means first to normalize the frequency difference
temp_summary <- compare_temps %>%
  mutate(datetime = as.POSIXct(datetime)) %>%
  # Create a 'date_hour' column to group by hour
  mutate(date_hour = floor_date(datetime, "hour"),
         date = as.Date(datetime)) %>%
  group_by(year, date, date_hour) %>%
  summarize(hourly_mean_temp = mean(Temperature, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Calculate "Hours Above" using the Hourly Means
hours_above <- temp_summary %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarize(
    hours_above_MMM = sum(hourly_mean_temp > 27.3, na.rm = TRUE),
    hours_above_Bleaching = sum(hourly_mean_temp > 28.3, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Calculate "Days Above" using Daily Maximums
days_above <- temp_summary %>%
  group_by(year, date) %>%
  summarize(daily_max = max(hourly_mean_temp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarize(
    days_above_MMM = sum(daily_max > 27.3, na.rm = TRUE),
    days_above_Bleaching = sum(daily_max > 28.3, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Combine and View Results
final_results <- left_join(hours_above, days_above, by = "year")
print(final_results)
```
